Proposition
[covariant derivative along a curve]

↗ def:dc-ch2-2-1 ↗ lem:dc-ch2-2-2-coord ↗ lem:dc-ch2-2-2-c-coord ↗ lem:dc-ch2-2-2-c-bridge

1. ch2:2.2Let $M$ carry an affine connection $ abla $, and let $c\colon I o M$ be a differentiable curve. There is a unique operation assigning to every vector field $V$ along $c$ a vector field $DV/dt$ along $c$ such that

  1. $ rac{D}{dt}(V+W)= rac{DV}{dt}+ rac{DW}{dt}$;

  2. $ rac{D}{dt}(fV)= rac{df}{dt}V+f rac{DV}{dt}$ for every differentiable $f\colon I o \mathbb {R}$;

  3. if $V(t)=Y(c(t))$ for $Y\in \mathcal{X}(M)$, then $ rac{DV}{dt}= abla _{dc/dt}Y$.

This operation is the covariant derivative along $c$.
Proof

\sketch In coordinates, write $V=\sum _jv^jX_j$, where $X_j= rac{\partial }{\partial x_j}(c(t))$. Properties (a)–(c) and section 1 force

\[ rac{DV}{dt} =\sum _j rac{dv^j}{dt}X_j +\sum _{i,j} rac{dx_i}{dt}v^j abla _{X_i}X_j. ag {1} \]

Thus the operation is unique. Conversely, formula (1) defines it locally and gives (a)–(c); uniqueness makes the local definitions agree on chart overlaps.

□
